title: Anchor skill at the visible-row crowd marginal
body:
## What changes

Skill is still `1 + log_score / R`, but the reference `R` is no longer the uniform guess. It is now the crowd marginal a participant can compute in each phase:

- **Phase 1**: per-item option shares of the `TRAIN` rows, scored on `DEV`.
- **Phase 2**: per-item option shares of the `TRAIN` + `DEV` rows, scored on `TEST`.

```
m_j[k] = (visible count of option k on item j + 0.5) / sum over options
m~_j   = floor + (1 - K_j * floor) * m_j
R      = -(mean over held-out cells of log m~_j[truth])
skill  = 1 + log_score / R
```

This is exactly the predictor in `baseline/marginal_counts`, so that baseline scores 0 in both phases. 1 is still perfect; a uniform guess is now well below 0.

## Consequences

- `R` depends on the data and differs between phases. It was a schema-only constant before.
- The phase-1 Laplace scale divides by the new `R`, which is smaller than the uniform reference, so the noise is somewhat larger. `R` is treated as a fixed constant of the release; the `privatize` docstring says what that leaves unaccounted.
- `score.py`: `marginal_reference()` added, `uniform_reference()` removed, `score()` takes the reference as an argument, and the log key is `marginal_reference`.
- README, the `config.yml` leaderboard comment, and the six tutorials are updated. The tutorial's crowd-baseline cell now prints skill `0.0000`.

## Needs a native-speaker check

The reworded tutorial strings in `fr`, `es`, `ru`, `zh` and `ar` (`k_and_gates`, `score_intro`, `lbl_skill_note`, `lbl_reference` in `tutorials/translations.yml`).

## Verification

`score.py --submission baseline/marginal_counts` on fresh sandboxes, un-noised skill from the organizer log:

| Instrument | Phase | skill | marginal_reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| sample | 1 | 0.0 | 0.892454 |
| sample | 2 | 0.0 | 0.909499 |
| unicef | 1 | 0.0 | 1.308458 |
| unicef | 2 | 0.0 | 1.318744 |
| world_bank | 1 | 0.0 | 1.536594 |
| world_bank | 2 | 0.0 | 1.529349 |

All six notebooks were rebuilt with `tutorials/build.py --force` and re-executed; outputs other than the scoring cell are unchanged.

title: Proofread Russian translation
body:
Native-speaker proofread of the Russian tutorial. All changes were made in the `ru` block of `tutorials/translations.yml`, with `tutorials/ru.ipynb` regenerated via `python tutorials/build.py` after each pass (unchanged cells keep their outputs; no other language is touched).

**Scope: the full notebook** — every key in the `ru` pack was reviewed against the English original.

Main kinds of changes:
- **Naturalness**: reworded sentences that read as literal translations (e.g. the class-system and gate-logic paragraphs, the section-2 intro, the bad-model discussion).
- **Terminology**: consistent survey-methodology vocabulary — «оцениваемая совокупность», «основа выборки», «опросные инструменты», «интервью» (for interviews/fieldwork), «условие перехода» (gate). "Prediction-powered inference" is kept in English where the concept is introduced.
- **Precision fixes**: restored details lost in translation (census roster, "whether anyone has a phone"), replaced «наты» with «(при натуральном логарифме)», clarified that `score.py` reads roles but never splits.
- **Table labels and printed strings** (`lbl_*`, `col_*`, `role_*`, docstrings) tightened for grammar; printf placeholders (`%.0f %%`, `%d`) preserved.
- **Formatting conventions preserved**: backticks on identifiers in markdown cells, plain text in code comments/docstrings (matching the English convention), original bold/italic emphasis carried over.

One deliberate small departure from the English: in the gate-logic paragraph the "free points" sentence is replaced with an explicit instruction that the model should put its probability on `NA_GATED` for determinable cells.

title: [small] Stray empty `main` file + placeholder text in rules
body:
Two small, cosmetic things noticed while reading the public harness — no code impact.

1. **Empty stray `main` file at the repo root.** There's a zero-byte file named
   `main` (no extension) at the top level. It looks accidentally committed —
   likely meant to be ignored or removed.

2. **Rules text still has placeholders.** In the README's Competition Rules,
   the data-provider list reads `[*list data-providing entities, e.g., the
   International Bank for Reconstruction and Development; [Provider 2];
   [Provider 3]*]`, so that section reads as not-yet-final.

Both are minor; filing together for tracking, not urgent.

title: In-process scoring lets predict() write to disk (PASS); make Docker the default worker

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: This will not be worked on

body:
## Summary

In the default in-process scoring mode, a submission's `predict()` can write to
the local filesystem and still score `PASS`. The README states `predict()` must
stay pure ("No files, no sockets, no processes"), and the network cut is
enforced, but the filesystem is not. On a reused worker this is the first half
of a two-submission exfiltration chain, and it side-steps the "no install hooks
that try to reach the underlying data" rule rather than catching it.

`--docker` mode already closes this. The suggestion is to make the container the
default on the scoring worker and treat the in-process path as a local
debugging convenience only.

## Repro

A minimal submission that writes the frame to disk and otherwise returns a valid
uniform prediction:

```python
# main.py
import numpy as np, pandas as pd

def predict(frame, schema):
    with open("/tmp/exfil_test.txt", "w") as fh:      # purity rule says no files
        fh.write(frame.to_json())
    items = [n for n, r in schema["items"].items()
             if r["class"] in ("GIVEN", "PREDICT")]
    opts = {n: len(schema["items"][n]["values"])
               + (1 if schema["items"][n].get("gate") else 0) for n in items}
    vals = frame[items].to_numpy(dtype=object)
    return [[1.0 / opts[n]] * opts[n]
            for i in range(vals.shape[0])
            for j, n in enumerate(items)
            if pd.isna(vals[i, j])]
```

```
$ python score.py --submission mysub --data _sandbox/sample \
                  --schema data/sample.json --phase 1
PASS  0.0000  (11.8s)
$ ls /tmp/exfil_test.txt
-rw-r--r--  1 user  staff  14064  /tmp/exfil_test.txt
```

The frame is now on the worker's disk, written by scored code that passed.

## Why it matters

`predict()` runs with the network already gone, so a single submission cannot
exfiltrate on its own. The concern is a reused worker across submissions:

1. Submission A writes the frame (or a summary of it) to a path outside the
   discarded work directory.
2. Submission B's **install step** runs with the network up and no data. It
   reads the file A left behind and posts it. An sdist in `requirements.txt`
   executes arbitrary `setup.py` at install time, so this needs no cooperation
   from `predict()` at all.

This is exactly the "must not include install hooks that try to reach the
underlying data" case in the rules. Right now the harness can punish it after
the fact but cannot prevent it in the default mode.

## Suggested fix

Run the scoring worker under the existing `--docker` path by default. It already
gives `--read-only`, a tmpfs `/tmp` that is discarded with the container, and
`--network=none` at the kernel — which turns the file-write into a no-op that
cannot persist across submissions. The in-process socket cut stays useful for
local iteration, just not as the grader of record.

A lighter-weight in-process hardening (redirecting writes to the work directory,
or a filesystem guard analogous to the socket patch) would narrow the gap but
would not match the guarantee the container already provides.

## Notes

This is an observation about the **public harness only** — `score.py` run
against the synthetic sandbox from `make_sandbox.py`. No competition microdata
was involved or touched. Filing per the disclosure guidance in the rules.
